Rashi on Zevachim 8a:10:1.hebrew: ולרבינא - דלא קשיא ליה אלא "עולת עולתו", ש"מנחתו" ו"נסכו" דכתיבי נמי גבי נזיר, אמאי לא קשיא ליה:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:10:1.english: And according to Ravina - [Ravina] is bothered only by “the burnt offering of his burnt offering”; [but regarding] “his meal offering” and “his libation,” which are also written regarding the Nazirite, why is he not bothered by them?:

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:11:1.hebrew: ההוא מיבעי ליה - כי היכי דדרשינן לכל מנחתם ונסכיהם, בלילה ואפי' למחר, שיוכשרו לבא למחר לבא בלילה — הכי נמי דרשינן להאי ועשה את מנחתו: כל זמן שיעשנו הוא קרוי מנחתו, ונסכו של זה, אע"פ שלא קרבו עם זבחו:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:11:1.english: That is necessary for it - Just as we expound with regard to every instance of “their meal offering and their libations” [that they may be brought] at night and even the next day, so that they are valid to come the next day [and] to come at night — so too we expound this [verse]: “and he shall prepare its meal offering” — whenever he prepares it, it is called his meal offering, and likewise the libation of this one, even though they were not sacrificed together with his animal offering:

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:12:1.hebrew: מי גמרי - שאר חטאות וחטאת נזיר מהדדי, דתמצי לומר חד למצוה וחד לעכב? סתם חטאת קרי חטאת חלב, משום דשכיחא טפי:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:12:1.english: Are they derived - [Are] the other sin offerings and the nazirite's sin offering [derived] from one another, such that you could say that one [applies] as a mitzvah [only] and the other as indispensable? An unspecified "sin offering" refers to the sin offering for forbidden fat, because it is more common.

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:12:2.hebrew: שכן כרת - מכפרת על חייבי כרת. אלמא לא גמרי מהדדי, וכיון דלא גמרי מהדדי, תרווייהו למצוה אצטריכו:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:12:2.english: Since [it involves] karet - It atones for those liable to karet. Evidently, they cannot be derived from one another; and since they cannot be derived from one another, both of them were needed for [teaching] the mitzvah.

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:14:1.hebrew: ואשכחן שנוי קדש - ולעכב, דהא נפקא לן מצוה לעיל בשאר חטאות:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:14:1.english: And we found [that] deviation [in the type of] sanctity - [disqualifies] and is indispensable, for we derived the commandment [of this] above regarding the other sin offerings:

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:14:2.hebrew: וכפר על המטהר - סיפיה דועשה הכהן את החטאת הוא ועל המטהר, אכולהו עשיות קאי:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:14:2.english: And make atonement for the one that is to be purified - The end of [the verse], “And the priest shall make the sin offering,” which is “and for the one that is to be purified,” refers to all the acts [of the sacrificial service].

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:17:1.english: And let it be derived from these - [From the sin offerings of] a nazirite and a leper.

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:18:1.hebrew: שאלה - נזיר נשאל לחכם ועוקר נזירתו, ופטור מן הקרבן:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:18:1.english: A request - A nazirite can make a request of a Sage [to dissolve his vow], and uproot his naziriteship, and he is exempt from the offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:19:1.hebrew: שכן אין באין בדלות גרסינן - שאין חטאות אלו יורדות בעניות להביא עוף:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:19:1.english: “For they do not come in poverty” is the text we read - For these sin offerings do not descend [in the case of] poverty to bring a bird.

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:1:1.english: And the priest shall take - It is an expression of receiving [i.e., collecting the blood].

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:21:1.hebrew: והנך קראי לעכב - וכשלמים: מה שלמים לא חלקת בהן למצוה, אף חטאת לא תחלוק בו לעכב. וכיון דכתיב עכובא בזריקה, אתיא להו לכולהו עבודות בהך דרשא מהיקשא דשלמים:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:21:1.english: And those verses [teach] to be indispensable - And [the law of the sin offering is derived] from a peace offering: Just as with a peace offering you did not distinguish between its [rites] with regard to the mitzva [ab initio], so too with a sin offering you should not distinguish with regard to [the rites] being indispensable. And since indispensability is written with regard to the sprinkling, all the [other] rites come by this teaching, from the analogy to the peace offering:

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:22:1.hebrew: אשכחן חטאת חלב דכתיב ביה לחטאת - "ושחט אותה לחטאת". בסתם חטאת כתיב "אם נפש כי תחטא" וגו':
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:22:1.english: We found [a source for] a sin offering of forbidden fat, as it is written regarding it "for a sin offering" - "And he shall slaughter it for a sin offering." Regarding an unspecified sin offering, it is written, "If a person sins," etc.

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:2:1.hebrew: וכפר - היינו בזריקה. הולכה לא אצטריך קרא, דבכלל קבלה היא, מתרביא ליה:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:2:1.english: And he shall atone - This refers to the sprinkling. For [the requirement of intent in] carrying [the blood], a verse is not needed, because it is included in collection; it is derived by extension from it.

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:4:1.hebrew: אשכחן למצוה כו' - ואי קשיא, מצוה מהיקשא דזאת התורה משלמים אתיא, כשאר כל הזבחים — אין הכי נמי. ומסקנא מהתם יליף לה לקמיה, ומעיקרא הוא דמהדרינן, דנכתבו כולהו בגופיה:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:4:1.english: We found [the source] for the mitzvah, etc. - And if one objects: the mitzvah [to sprinkle for the sake of the owner] comes from the analogy of "this is the law" [stated regarding] the peace offerings, like all the other sacrifices — indeed so. And in the conclusion, [the Gemara] derives it from there later; but at the beginning it is that we are searching for [a source] in which all of them are written in the [offering's] own case.

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:4:2.hebrew: כדאמר רב הונא כו' - לקמן בשמעתין:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:4:2.english: As Rav Huna says, etc. - Below, in this sugya.

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:4:3.hebrew: חטאתו - "וכפר עליו הכהן מחטאתו" (כשזרק דמו לשמו חטאת חטאתו). מדהוה ליה למכתב "מחטאת", וכתיב וי"ו יתירא, למדרש בה לשם בעלים:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:4:3.english: His sin offering - "And the priest shall atone for him from his sin" (when he sprinkled its blood for its sake: sin offering, "his sin offering"). Since [the verse] should have written "from a sin offering," yet an extra letter vav is written, [this serves] to derive from it that the offering must be sacrificed for the sake of the owners:

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:5:1.hebrew: אשכחן מצוה בשנוי קדש - בכל עבודות. וזריקה אשכחן בה מצוה ועכוב בשנוי בעלים, דהאי ״מחטאתו״ נמי בזריקה כתיב, שהיא הכפרה:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:5:1.english: We found a mitzva with regard to a change of sanctity - in all the sacrificial rites. And with regard to sprinkling, we found in it both a mitzva and indispensability with regard to a change of owner, since this [phrase] "from his sin offering" is also written with regard to sprinkling, which is the atonement:

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:5:2.hebrew: לעכב בכל עבודות בשנוי קדש - שלא למדנו לאחד מהן. ושאר עבודות, לבד מזריקה, בשנוי בעלים, בין למצוה בין לעכב — מנלן:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:5:2.english: To be indispensable for all rites with regard to deviation of the offering's sanctity - For we have not derived it for any one of them. And [from where do we derive that] the other rites, apart from sprinkling, [performed] with deviation with regard to the owner, are [a requirement] both as a mitzva and as indispensable — from where do we know this?

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:6:1.hebrew: שיהו כל עשיותיו לשם חטאת - ולמצוה לא אצטריך קרא, דהא נפקא לן משאר חטאות, והאי לעכובא:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:6:1.english: That all of its actions must be for the sake of a sin offering - And for [the sake of] the mitzvah [i.e., as an initial requirement], the verse is not needed, since we derive it from the other sin offerings; and this [verse] teaches that it is indispensable [i.e., if not done for the sake of a sin offering, it is invalid].

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:7:1.hebrew: [<abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr> בס"א] אשכחן שנוי קדש, שנוי בעלים מנלן:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:7:1.english: [Thus we read, in the variant text (ס"א):] We found that there is a requirement regarding a change of sanctity; but a change of owners, from where do we derive it?

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:8:1.hebrew: אמר רב הונא כו' - גבי נזיר כתיב ועשה את חטאתו ואת עולתו, הרי חטאתו למצוה, וכשלמים. מה שלמים לא חלקת בהן בין זריקה לשאר עבודות בשנוי בעלים למצוה, אף חטאת לא תחלק בין זריקה לשאר עבודות לעכב. הרי לך מצוה ועכוב בין בשנוי קדש בין בשנוי בעלים. כך נ"ל, וכן יש לפרש גבי חטאת מצורע לקמן נ"ל:
Rashi on Zevachim 8a:8:1.english: Rav Huna said, etc. - Regarding a nazirite it is written, “And he shall offer his sin offering and his burnt offering.” Thus [the sin offering] is [required] as a mitzvah (i.e., ab initio), and [it is compared] to peace offerings. Just as with peace offerings you do not distinguish between the throwing [of the blood] and the other services, [in that a change of] owners [disqualifies] as a mitzvah, so too with a sin offering, do not distinguish between the throwing and the other services, [so that it is disqualified] to the point of preventing [fulfillment]. Thus you have both a mitzvah and a disqualification, whether with a change of sanctity or a change of owners. So it seems to me; and so too one should explain regarding the sin offering of a leper, below. So it seems to me.

Tosafot on Zevachim 8a:11:1.hebrew: מנחתם ונסכיהם בלילה, מנחתם ונסכיהם אפי' למחר - לאו מהאי קרא [קדריש]:
Tosafot on Zevachim 8a:11:1.english: "Their meal offering and their libations" at night; "their meal offering and their libations" even on the next day - [This] is not derived from this verse [i.e., the verse about the nazirite].

Tosafot on Zevachim 8a:21:1.hebrew: הילכך מצוה משלמים והנך קראי לעכב - וא"ת: למה לי למכתב בכולהו? לכתוב בהך, ואינך כולהו אתו מדכתיב "זאת תורת החטאת" — תורה אחת לכל החטאות, כדלקמן בשמעתא דמבוג. ויש לומר דבמסקנא לא קאי. ואע"ג דבפרק דם חטאת (לקמן זבחים דף צב.) תנן "תורה אחת לכל החטאות" — היינו במילתא דכתיבא התם: "אשר יזה מדמה על הבגד". ומיהו איכא דאית ליה הך סברא, לר' שמעון, בריש מסכת מנחות (דף ג:). וא"ת: למה לי למכתב בחטאת חלב עכובא בכל עבודות? לכתוב בחדא, ונימא: מה שלמים לא חלקת למצוה, אף חטאת לא תחלוק, כדקאמר לעיל. וי"ל דכי האי גוונא זמנין דטרח ליה קרא וכתב, א"נ אתי לדרשא אחרינא. וא"ת: מנא לן בחטאת נזיר עכובא בשנוי בעלים? ויש לומר: מ"חטאת" "חטאתו". אע"ג דלעיל לא קאי, עיקר פירכא סמיך אותו; מי גמירי מהדדי:
Tosafot on Zevachim 8a:21:1.english: Therefore the mitzvah [is derived] from peace offerings, and those verses are to make it indispensable - And if you ask: Why did I need it written for all of them? Let it be written for this one, and all the others would derive it from the verse "This is the law of the sin offering" — one law for all sin offerings, as [stated] below in the passage of "Mevug"? And one may say that in the conclusion [of the passage] this does not stand. And although in the chapter "Dam Chatat" (below, Zevachim 92a) we learned "one law for all sin offerings," that refers to a matter written there: "that which was sprinkled from its blood onto the garment." Nevertheless, there is one who holds this reasoning — Rabbi Shimon, at the beginning of tractate Menachot (3b). And if you ask: Why did I need it written for the sin offering of fat (chelev) that it is indispensable in all the services? Let it be written for one, and we would say: Just as peace offerings you did not divide with respect to the mitzvah, so too the sin offering you should not divide, as [the Gemara] said above? And one may say that in a case like this, sometimes the verse goes to the trouble and writes [it], or alternatively it comes for a different exposition. And if you ask: From where do we know that for the sin offering of a nazirite, [the sacrifice is] indispensable with regard to a change of owners? And one may say: from [the repetition of] "sin offering" [and] "his sin offering." Although [the Gemara] above does not stand [on this], the main refutation is supported by it; [the offerings] were not learned from one another.

Tosafot on Zevachim 8a:3:1.hebrew: זריקה מנלן מוכפר עליו הכהן מחטאתו - הרבה יש תימה: דהני קראי דשחיטה וקבלה — "ושחט אותה לחטאת", "ולקח הכהן" — כתיבי בסתם חטאת, כגון חטאת חלב בפרשת ויקרא גבי כשבה. והאי קרא דוכפר עליו הכהן מחטאתו כתיב בחטאת דשמיעת קול וביטוי שפתים; אבל בחטאת חלב לא כתיב "מחטאתו" אלא "על חטאתו" כתיב. ובתורת כהנים באותה פרשה עצמה דחטאת חלב דריש מקרא דמחטאתו, אע"ג דלא כתיב בההיא פרשתא. וזהו תימה, דשביק קרא דעל חטאתו דכתיב בההיא פרשתא! ושמא משום דעל חטאתו לאחר הקטרת אימורים הוא דכתיב. אבל תימה: דלקמן משמע דכל הני קראי דהכא בחטאת חלב כתיבי, דקאמר "אשכחנא חטאת חלב, אבל חטאת דשמיעת קול וביטוי שפתים מנא לן"? וי"ל דהכי קאמר לקמן: אשכחנא חטאת חלב עכובא שחיטה וקבלה בשנוי קדש, ושאר עבודות נילף, כדאמר לעיל: מה שלמים לא חלקת בין זביחה לשאר עבודות למצוה, אף כאן לא תחלוק לעכב; וקבלה נמי לא הוצרך לכתוב. אבל שמיעת קול מנא לן? דאע"ג דכתיב ביה "וכפר עליו מחטאתו" ודרשינן לעיל "לשם חטאת", היינו שנוי קדש בזריקה, ולא חלקת לא נימא בזריקה, לפי שהיא עיקר כפרה. ושנוי בעלים בחטאת חלב נגמר משמיעת קול, דליכא פירכא. וי"מ דמחטאתו דקאמר היינו בשעיר נשיא, דכתיב ביה נמי "מחטאתו", וקאי גם אחטאת חלב. וקשה, דכתיב לאחר הקטרת אימורים. נראה לי ברו"ך. ועוד נ"ל דלא הוה מצי למדרש מ"וכפר על חטאתו אשר חטא" דכתיב בחטאת חלב, משום דהכי קאמר "על פשעו אשר חטא" (ולא בשמיעת קול מיירי בחטאת קרבנו), ולא משעיר נשיא דכתיב "מחטאתו ונסלח לו", והיינו "מפשעו", וחטאתו שלו, "ונסלח לו". אבל בשמיעת קול לא כתיב זה ולא זו, אלא "מחטאתו", היינו מקרבנו. ברו"ך:
Tosafot on Zevachim 8a:3:1.english: From where do we derive [the law of] the throwing [of the blood]? "And the priest shall make atonement for him from his sin" - There is much to wonder about: These verses concerning slaughtering and receiving — "And he shall slaughter it for a sin offering," "And the priest shall take" — are written about an unspecified sin offering, such as the fat-sin-offering in the section of Vayikra regarding the lamb. But this verse, "And the priest shall make atonement for him from his sin," is written regarding the sin offering for hearing a voice [of adjuration] and for utterance of the lips; but regarding the fat-sin-offering, "from his sin" is not written, but rather "for his sin." And in the Torat Kohanim, in that very section of the fat-sin-offering, [the Sages] expound from the verse "from his sin," even though it is not written in that section. And this is astonishing, for [the Sages] leave aside the verse "for his sin" that is written in that very section! Perhaps it is because "for his sin" is written after the burning of the sacrificial portions. But there is [another] difficulty: later [the Gemara] implies that all these verses here are written regarding the fat-sin-offering, as it says, "We have found the fat-sin-offering; but the sin offering for hearing a voice and for utterance of the lips, from where do we know it?" And one can answer that this is what [the Gemara] says later: We have found, regarding the fat-sin-offering, that slaughtering and receiving are indispensable in the case of deviation from the type of offering, and we derive the other services, as stated above: Just as [with] a peace offering, you did not distinguish between slaughtering and the other services as to the ideal [performance], so too here, do not distinguish as to indispensability; and receiving, too, did not need to be written. But [for] the sin offering for hearing a voice, from where do we know it? For even though it is written regarding it, "and he shall make atonement for him from his sin," and we expound above [that this means] "for the sake of a sin offering," that is deviation from the type of offering in the throwing — [still,] "you did not distinguish" cannot be said regarding the throwing, because it is the essence of atonement. And deviation regarding the owner in the fat-sin-offering is learned from the sin offering for hearing a voice, for there is no refutation. Some explain that "from his sin" that [the Gemara] says refers to the ruler's goat, regarding which "from his sin" is also written, and it applies also to the fat-sin-offering. But this is difficult, for it is written after the burning of the sacrificial portions. It seems to me, Baruch. And further it seems to me that [the Gemara] could not expound from "and he shall make atonement for his sin that he sinned," which is written regarding the fat-sin-offering, because this is what it says, "for his transgression that he sinned" (and it does not speak of the hearing-a-voice offering, but of his own sin offering), and not from the ruler's goat, where it is written "from his sin, and it shall be forgiven him," which is "from his transgression," and his sin offering is his own, "and it shall be forgiven him." But regarding the hearing-a-voice offering, neither this nor that is written, but rather "from his sin," meaning from his offering. Baruch.

Tosafot on Zevachim 8a:5:1.hebrew: וזריקה בשנוי בעלים בין למצוה בין לעכב - תימה: דמהאי קרא "וכפר עליו הכהן מחטאתו" דרשינן תרווייהו, זריקה בשנוי קדש ושנוי בעלים; ואם כן, מחטאת חטאתו תיפוק ליה נמי עכובא בשנוי קדש, כמו בשנוי בעלים, דאתרווייהו קאי:
Tosafot on Zevachim 8a:5:1.english: "And sprinkling with a change of owner, both as a mitzvah and as indispensable" - This is difficult: for from this verse, "And the priest shall atone for him for his sin offering" (Leviticus 4:26), we derive both [laws] with regard to sprinkling — [a change of] sanctity and [a change of] owner. If so, from "from his sin offering" [we should be able to] derive indispensability for a change of sanctity as well, just as for a change of owner, since [the verse] refers to both:

Tosafot on Zevachim 8a:6:1.hebrew: ועשה את חטאתו שיהו כל עשיותיו לשם חטאת. אשכחנא שנוי קדש, שנוי בעלים מנ"ל? אמר רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: חטאת חטאתו - כך גירסת הקונטרס, ולגירסא זו מוקי ברישא לעכב בשנוי קדש, קודם שנעמיד למצוה בשנוי בעלים באם אינו ענין. ואינו משמע כן בכולי פירקא לעיל גבי שלמים ופסח, דקאמר: אשכחנא שנוי קדש, שנוי בעלים מנא לן? ומוקי ברישא בשנוי בעלים באם אינו ענין, קודם שיעמיד קרא לעכב. ומיהו י"ל דשאני הכא, דכבר אשכחנא קרא לזריקה בשנוי בעלים. ואית ספרים דגרסי: אם אינו ענין לשנוי קדש, דנפקא ליה מהתם, תניהו ענין לשנוי בעלים. אשכחנא, למצוה לעכב מנא לן? אמר רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: חטאת חטאתו. ולגירסא זו לא צריכינן תו לקרא דלעיל בזריקה, וניחא נמי הא דגרסינן לעיל "כדאמר רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע חטאת חטאתו", דמשמע דעיקר מילתא לא אתמר אההיא, והיינו משום דלבסוף לא קיימא:
Tosafot on Zevachim 8a:6:1.english: "And he shall offer his sin offering" — that all its actions must be for the sake of a sin offering. We have found [the case of] a change of sanctity; [as for] a change of owner, from where do we know it? Rav Huna the son of Rav Yehoshua said: "Sin offering" — "his sin offering" - This is the reading of the Kuntres (Rashi). According to this reading, [the Gemara] interprets in the first clause [that the verse] is to render [the offering] invalid in a case of a change of sanctity, before we have established [the verse] as a commandment [that applies] to a change of owner, by [the principle of] "if it is not needed for its own subject." But this is not implied throughout this chapter above, regarding peace offerings and the Paschal offering, where [the Gemara] says: "We have found [the case of] a change of sanctity; a change of owner, from where do we know it?" And [there] it interprets in the first clause [the verse as referring] to a change of owner, by [the principle of] "if it is not needed for its own subject," before it establishes the verse to render [the offering] invalid. However, one can say that here is different, for we have already found a verse for the throwing of the blood in a case of a change of owner. And there are books that read: "If it is not needed for its own subject" — [namely] a change of sanctity, which is derived from there — "establish it as [applying to] a change of owner." [Then the question is:] We have found [the law as] a commandment; that it is invalidating, from where do we know it? Rav Huna the son of Rav Yehoshua said: "Sin offering" — "his sin offering." And according to this reading, we no longer need the verse above regarding throwing [the blood], and it also fits well what we read above, "as Rav Huna the son of Rav Yehoshua said: 'Sin offering' — 'his sin offering,'" which implies that the main point was not stated regarding that [case], and this is because ultimately it does not stand:
